ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Wind energy is a renewable and clean energy source. A small wind power station has been built in a remote area of a county to supply electricity to the industrial park users in the county. The schematic diagram of the power transmission process is shown in the figure. The generator output power is $P = 200\,\mathrm{kW}$, the output voltage is $500\,\mathrm{V}$, and the total resistance of the transmission line is $R = 20\,\Omega$. The allowable power loss in the line is $1\%$ of the output power, and the required voltage for the users is $220\,\mathrm{V}$.

1. What is the turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of the step-up transformer used? (Neglecting the losses of the transformer)
2. What is the turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of the step-down transformer used? (Neglecting the losses of the transformer)

A small wind power station has been built in a remote area of a county to supply electricity to the industrial park users in the county. The generator output power is $P = 200\,\mathrm{kW}$, the output voltage is $500\,\mathrm{V}$, and the total resistance of the transmission line is $R = 20\,\Omega$. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the circuit from left to right is respectively a generator, a step-up transformer, a transmission line with total resistance R, a step-down transformer, and a user load. The coil on the left side of the step-up transformer is labeled n1, and the coil on the right side is labeled n2; the transmission line is marked with resistance R; the coil on the left side of the step-down transformer is labeled n3, and the coil on the right side is labeled n4, with the right end connected to the user. Reasoning: The allowed power loss on the transmission line is 1% of the output power, so P_loss = 0.01 × 200 kW = 2 kW = 2000 W. From P_loss = I^2 R, and R = 20 Ω, obtain I = sqrt(2000/20) = 10 A. The ideal step-up transformer has no loss, and the power transmitted to the line is 200 kW, therefore the output voltage of the secondary coil of the step-up transformer V2 = P/I = 200000/10 = 20000 V. The generator output voltage is the voltage of the primary coil of the step-up transformer V1 = 500 V, so n1/n2 = V1/V2 = 500/20000 = 1/40. The voltage loss on the transmission line is IR = 10 × 20 = 200 V, therefore the voltage of the primary coil of the step-down transformer V3 = 20000 - 200 = 19800 V. The voltage required by the user is the voltage of the secondary coil of the step-down transformer V4 = 220 V, so n3/n4 = V3/V4 = 19800/220 = 90/1.
